'''Avner Friedman''' ({{langx|he|אבנר פרידמן}}; born November 19, 1932) is Distinguished Professor of [[Mathematics]] and Physical Sciences at [[Ohio State University]]. His primary field of research is [[partial differential equations]], with interests in [[stochastic processes]], [[mathematical modeling]], [[free boundary problem]]s, and [[control theory]].

Friedman received his Ph.D. degree in 1956 from the [[Hebrew University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=10279}}</ref> He was a professor of mathematics at [[Northwestern University]] (1962&ndash;1985), a Duncan Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[Purdue University]] (1985&ndash;1987), and a professor of mathematics (Regents' Professor from 1996) at the [[University of Minnesota]] (1987&ndash;2001). He was director of the Institute for Mathematics and its Applications from 1987 to 1997.  He was the founding director of [https://cse.umn.edu/math/minnesota-center-industrial-mathematics Minnesota Center for Industrial Mathematics] (1994–2001). He was the founding director of the [[Mathematical Biosciences Institute]] at [[Ohio State University]], serving as its first director from 2002&ndash;2008.

Friedman has been the chair of the [[Board of Mathematical Sciences]] (1994&ndash;1997) and the president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (1993&ndash;1994).<ref>SIAM Presidents http://www.siam.org/about/more/presidents.php</ref> He has been awarded the [[Sloan Fellowship]] (1962&ndash;65), the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1966&ndash;7), the [[Stampacchia Prize]] (1982), the [[National Science Foundation]] Special Creativity Award (1983&ndash;85; 1991&ndash;93). He is a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (since 1987) and a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (since 1993). In 2009 he became a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref>SIAM Fellows http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=last</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-12-29.</ref>

He has been adviser to 27 doctoral students<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=10279 |title=Avner Friedman - the Mathematics Genealogy Project |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |access-date=26 May 2018}}</ref> and has published 25 books<ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.math.osu.edu/friedman.158/FRIEDMANlongvita.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae |website=people.math.osu.edu |access-date=2019-03-10}}</ref> and over 500 papers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.math.osu.edu/friedman.158/friedmanbibli.html |title=Bibliography |website=people.math.osu.edu |access-date=2019-03-10}}</ref>
